newsitem.title: USA: GTE unit told workers to shred papers-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GTE unit told workers to shred papers-WSJ.

text.p: According to papers filed in a suit in a state court, management at GTE Corp's California unit told workers to shred documents which were at the center of a regulatory probe into fraudulent billing practices, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.

In a case that goes back to the middle of 1992, GTE has said a special business unit set up to market services to Spanish speaking customers billed for calling services which were not ordered, the newspaper said.
Workers associated with the actions were subsequently fired, the newspaper said.

The Journal said in the latest motions filed in a California state court, both a current and former worker said GTE knew about the fraud two years before it admitted the activities to state regulators.
According to a court documents, a transcript indicated some employees were recommended to shred key papers by some, the Journal said.

GTE was quoted in the the newspaper as saying it immediately took action when it uncovered inappropriate sales tactics. As for allegations of document shredding, GTE was quoted as saying it had not seen evidence workers were told to destroy documents but "it takes the allegations very seriously and will fully investigate the matter."
GTE was not immediately available to comment further on the report.
